title: An Invariant Learning Characterization of Controlled Text Generation

bias_targets.methodology: Partitioning training data into environments based on the sum of identity attributes (including race, gender, religion, sexual orientation, and disability) to evaluate and mitigate spurious correlations between demographic terms and toxicity predictions.
Manipulating the grammatical correctness of text to synthetically induce a spurious correlation with toxicity, testing whether models generalize out-of-distribution without relying on grammar.

Measuring the out-of-distribution generalization and robustness of toxicity classifiers across different text distributions generated by prompting language models with RealToxicityPrompts and various profession-based personification templates.
